title: Inverse image of the coefficient sheaves
statement:
Because all coefficient sheaves are pulled back from the point, they are compatible with
inverse image. The same holds for their Tate twists ([sk-def-sp-tate-twist]), and a finite
extension of coefficient fields gives a finite free extension of coefficient sheaves.

Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes. Coefficient sheaves are the
pullbacks of condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. The admissible
coefficients are the finite commutative coefficient rings $A$ and
$\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb$. Give $A$ its discrete topology. The rings
$A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$ are condensed as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; the $\Qlb$ coefficient is specifically
the condensed ring of continuous maps taking values in some finite subextension,
as defined in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed];
$E$ and $F$ below are finite subextensions of $\Qlb/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
The assertions about Tate twists are made on the domain of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]:
$\ell$ is invertible on $X$ and $Y$, and a finite coefficient ring $A$ being twisted
is annihilated by a power of $\ell$. No such invertibility assumption is imposed
on the untwisted assertions.

1. For every admissible $\Lambda$, the canonical map
   $$
   f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\longrightarrow\Lambda_X
   $$
   is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (this is the map $\alpha_f$
   of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). For every integer $d$, its Tate twists have the corresponding canonical
   isomorphism of coefficient module sheaves
   $f^{-1}(\Lambda_Y(d))\cong\Lambda_X(d)$ along $\alpha_f$, including the twists
   of a finite ring $A$.
2. If $E\subset F$ is a finite extension, then $\cO_{F,X}$ is a finite free
   $\cO_{E,X}$-module and $F_X$ is a finite free $E_X$-module.

By (1), the pullback $f^*\colon\Mod(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
of modules over these sheaves is exact. More precisely, it is canonically naturally
isomorphic to the lift of $f^{-1}$ whose underlying sheaf functor is $f^{-1}$
and whose $\Lambda_X$-action is obtained using $\alpha_f^{-1}$.

proof.text: For a condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$, use the monoidal natural isomorphism $f^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. Its component is precisely $\alpha_f$ by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], and [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] states that this component is invertible. The coefficient-morphism statement also identifies it as an isomorphism of ring objects, so this proves the displayed comparison as a map of sheaves of rings, uniformly for all admissible coefficients, including finite rings.

For the twist assertion, $\ell$ is invertible on both schemes and the coefficient belongs to the list in [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists]. Apply its comparison $f^{-1}(\Lambda_Y(d))\cong\Lambda_X(d)$ for every integer $d$. This is compatible with the same $\alpha_f$ and the module structures, as required to interpret it as the twisted coefficient comparison. Its list includes the finite $\ell$-power-torsion rings $A$. Thus it proves exactly the Tate-twist portion of (1) on the domain where those twists were defined.

For $E\subset F$ finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $d=[F:E]$, choose an $\cO_E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\cO_F$ using [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. With that basis, [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] supplies the basis-induced isomorphisms $\cO_{E,X}^{\,d}\cong\cO_{F,X}$ and $E_X^{\,d}\cong F_X$. These are isomorphisms of modules over the respective coefficient sheaves, for arbitrary $X$. A module is finite free of rank $d$ precisely when it is isomorphic to the direct sum of $d$ copies of its ring; hence these two displayed isomorphisms prove (2). No flatness converse or claim that inverse image commutes with arbitrary inverse limits is used.

We check the category hypotheses needed for the final exactness assertion. Work with the small skeletons of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$ fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] with the constant sheaf of rings $\mathbf Z$: a sheaf of abelian groups has the unique $\mathbf Z$-action $n\cdot m$ by repeated addition (for a section of the constant integer sheaf, define this locally where that section is constant and glue), so this identifies its module category with $\Sh(-,\Ab)$ and makes the latter abelian with equalizers and coequalizers. The tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is closed symmetric monoidal, and [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-closed] says that tensoring in either variable is additive and preserves all colimits. In particular tensoring with either coefficient ring preserves finite colimits. The pulled-back coefficient rings are commutative monoid objects by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Consequently [lem-sfb-modobj-abelian] makes both categories of coefficient module objects abelian. These checks also give all the closedness, braiding and colimit hypotheses for extension along an invertible coefficient map in the next step.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-module-upper-star], module pullback is $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$. Step 1 makes $\alpha_f$ invertible. The source ring $f^{-1}\Lambda_Y$ is commutative since it is isomorphic as a ring object to the commutative $\Lambda_X$. Thus step 4 and this observation supply the hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso], so it is naturally isomorphic to $G=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$. Explicitly, if the transported action on $f^{-1}M$ is $\widetilde\gamma:f^{-1}\Lambda_Y\otimes f^{-1}M\to f^{-1}M$, its $\Lambda_X$-action under $G$ is $\widetilde\gamma\circ(\alpha_f^{-1}\otimes1)$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], restriction changes only this action, leaving all underlying objects and arrows unchanged. Hence, for the two forgetful functors, $U_XG=f^{-1}U_Y$ literally; this states precisely in what sense module pullback is the sheaf inverse-image functor.

source.place: final sentence of the statement; scalar extension in def-sfb-module-upper-star and def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso

proof.text: The abelian sheaf inverse image $f^{-1}$ is exact by clause 4 of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. By clause 3 it preserves finite limits of underlying sheaves of sets. Since clause 4 computes abelian inverse image on those underlying sheaves, it preserves the zero abelian sheaf (whose underlying sheaf is terminal) and binary products with their projections. The canonical injections into a binary biproduct are the product maps with components identity and zero; zero maps factor through the zero object. Hence it also preserves these injections. It preserves the diagonal by the product universal property and the codiagonal by the coproduct universal property of the same finite biproduct. For $h,k:M\to N$, applying it to $h+k=\nabla_N\circ(h\oplus k)\circ\Delta_M$ therefore gives $f^{-1}(h+k)=f^{-1}h+f^{-1}k$, proving additivity. Apply [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] to $\mathcal C=\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal D=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$, $\mathcal R=\Lambda_Y$, $\mathcal S=\Lambda_X$, $F=f^{-1}$ and the functor $G$ of step 5. Step 4 verifies the abelian, additive monoidal and right-exact tensor hypotheses, and step 5 verifies the required equality of underlying functors. Thus $G$ is additive and exact. The natural isomorphism $f^*\cong G$ of step 5 identifies their kernel and cokernel diagrams by its invertible components, so $f^*$ is exact too. This proves the final assertion for every untwisted admissible coefficient without any invertibility condition on $\ell$ in the schemes.
